results.question: find an anchor for fiat on-ramp in Africa
results.answer: Yellow Card is Africa's largest licensed stablecoin fiat on-ramp and off-ramp, operating across 20 countries and converting local African currencies to and from USDC on Stellar [9]. Honey Coin provides another African fiat-to-stablecoin anchor headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, settling USDC/USDT on- and off-ramps across 18+ African markets via mobile money and bank rails [5]. Fonbnk is also a fiat on-ramp and off-ramp anchor on Stellar that converts local currency and prepaid mobile airtime into USDC for mobile-first, cash-based markets across Africa [10].

results.question: which wallets support Stellar
results.answer: Several wallets support Stellar, including Hana, a non-custodial multi-chain wallet available as a browser extension and mobile app [2]. Beans is a non-custodial Stellar wallet and money-transfer app for iOS and Android [3], while Decaf operates on both Solana and Stellar networks for cross-border transfers [4]. Hardware wallets like Ledger and Trezor also support Stellar (XLM) [5][6], and HOT Wallet is a non-custodial multichain wallet delivered as a Telegram mini-app and mobile app with native Stellar support [7].

results.question: tell me about Blend

results.question: what is SEP-41
results.answer: SEP-41 is the Soroban Token Interface standard that defines fully customizable contract tokens deployed as Wasm contracts [6][7]. These tokens implement their own storage and logic, can be held by both account types without requiring trustlines, and are commonly used when custom logic is needed such as mint/burn rules, vesting, or hooks [7]. SEP-41 tokens are also used as underlying assets for other blockchain standards like tokenized vaults [9].

results.question: how does the Stellar consensus protocol work
results.answer: The Stellar Consensus Protocol (SCP) is a proof of agreement protocol that enables consensus and validates transactions on the network [12]. SCP uses a federated Byzantine agreement (FBA) model that achieves robustness through quorum slices—individual trust decisions made by each node that together determine system-level quorums [11]. Nodes reach consensus, apply transaction sets, and update the ledger using Stellar Core, with consensus typically occurring every 5-7 seconds [14]. The protocol determines the final transaction set through a nomination and voting process across the validator network [16].

results.question: what is a trustline
results.answer: A trustline is a ledger entry on the Stellar network that allows an account to hold and trade a specific asset [9]. Trustlines must be created before an account can receive or hold non-native Stellar assets, and they can be authorized or unauthorized depending on the asset issuer's settings [7]. Users can manage trustlines through Stellar wallets and interfaces, and removing all trustlines is necessary before merging or closing a Stellar account [5].
